title: A harmonic gravity-gate pulse is source-reported; compatible hardware and noise remain open
status_authority: Exact receipt-selected Ultra return is preserved. The source-reported pulse and review statements are not upgraded by byte preservation or integration; no independent scientific review or physical validation was performed here.
reported_status: The Ultra return reports a constructed harmonic two-probe gravity-gate pulse, central algebra checks, and an independent Sol review. It also reports that the force, low trap frequency and isolation have not been demonstrated together; under its continuous independent stationary high-temperature Ohmic model, even a transplanted Q gives no credible gate regime. Strong prior work limits the novelty claim. No new physical capability is established.
scientific_scope_status: Within the source’s stable equal-frequency harmonic model, endpoint-flat control gives a conditional oscillator response and a ZZ phase, with probe/mechanics factorization but not arbitrary mechanical-state return. The scoped continuous independent stationary high-temperature Ohmic comparison gives |theta_sym| <= epsilon sqrt(Gamma_1 Gamma_2)/4. Its hypothetical benchmark assumes unmeasured force, low trap frequency, quality factor and isolation; the estimated epsilon is about 3e-9 under the granted Q. Rare-collision conditions and higher Newtonian thermal terms remain open. Mathematical correctness, novelty, physical feasibility and advantage remain UNKNOWN.

proof_availability.classification_scope: The complete serialized return, including its root response and embedded support-return evidence, is preserved with the selection receipt.
